text:
Aditya: quick sync — we need to pick a direction for the internal API shape for the new routing service. rest-first or gRPC-first? thoughts?
Maria: +1 to having a single opinion but happy to hear tradeoffs. what's the must-have for the service?
Aditya: must-haves: sub-50ms p50 for routing decisions, streaming for long-running evals, easy client libs for platform teams, good telemetry + quota propagation.
Sam: gRPC wins on typed contracts and streaming. protobufs give us clear schema evolution rules.
Jen: browser clients are real tho. if we go gRPC we either need grpc-web or a gateway layer. That adds ops overhead.
Leo: also consider our console and webhooks — they prefer JSON. We can't make every product team adopt proto.
Maria: could we do gRPC internally and expose REST at the edge? gateway/transcoding does that. But careful: transcoding can hide semantic mismatches.
Sam: +1. If we do gRPC-internal + JSON-external we should keep the gateway strict (no lossy mappings). e.g., enums -> strings, but avoid mapping oneof to loose objects.
Aditya: cost and latency of the gateway are concerns. We need a pattern: 1) grpc core, 2) lightweight proxy for browser, 3) sidecar for legacy services?
Jen: what about a polyglot approach: let teams choose gRPC or REST for their service, and have a typed adapter service (translation) per domain. avoids central gateway bottleneck.
Maria: downside: more adapters to maintain and inconsistent telemetry unless we standardize headers and tracing.
Leo: telemetry note — any translation layer must preserve token/quota headers: x-rd-user, x-rd-quota, traceparent. We lose attribution otherwise.
Sam: example proto snippet for routing api:
```proto
service Router {
  rpc Route(Request) returns (stream RouteEvent);
}
message Request {
  string model = 1;
  map<string,string> context = 2;
}
message RouteEvent {
  oneof payload { Decision decision = 1; LogEntry log = 2; }
}
```
Jen: streaming is nice for pushy signals, but many clients just want a single decision. we need unary endpoints too. don't force everyone to handle streams.
Aditya: rollout and UX: console teams want per-route telemetry and gradual rollout controls (canary %, model variant fallback). Does either transport make that easier?
Maria: they are orthogonal. telemetry and rollouts are higher-level. But gRPC gives us richer typed metadata to base rules on (e.g., structured attributes instead of JSON parsing).
Leo: quotas: our quota system expects a canonical resource string. Gateway JSON->proto mapping must emit that. otherwise quota evasion bugs will happen.
Sam: ops cost: supporting grpc-web + mTLS for internal + plaintext for sidecars is a lot. We could standardize on HTTP/2 with TLS everywhere, and expose grpc-web on the edge via Envoy.
Jen: Envoy solves a lot: transcoding filter, grpc-web support, header mutation. But it complicates local dev. We should provide a dev proxy Docker image.
Aditya: perf testing: can someone run a small benchmark comparing: (A) grpc core w/ direct client, (B) grpc core behind envoy transcoder, (C) rest-json direct. target: 64B requests, 1k qps, 95th latency. Sam?
Sam: I can run it. timeline?
Aditya: end of week would be ideal. keep it lightweight.
Maria: decision criteria proposal: 1) latency overhead (p95 increase), 2) developer ergonomics (client libs + browser), 3) operational surface (Envoy + adapters), 4) telemetry fidelity (header preservation + structured attrs). rank them and we decide.
Leo: plus constraint: no loss of quota attribution. that's a hard veto.
Jen: small UX ask: console wants consistent error shapes. With gRPC we get status codes and metadata; with JSON we need an error schema. Gateway must translate grpc Status -> JSON error cleanly.
Sam: also consider protobuf JSON mapping differences (e.g., default values omitted). If the console relies on presence of fields, we need explicit modeling.
Aditya: ok plan: Sam will run perf tests (A/B/C), I'll draft a short RFC with the decision criteria and a recommended path (likely gRPC-internal + Envoy edge + small translator sidecars for legacy teams). Maria/Jen/Leo please comment on the RFC.
deploy-bot: (automated) new draft created: link: https://rfd.internal/redwood/2466-routing-api-shape — reviewers: @Maria @Jen @Leo @Sam @Aditya :eyes:
Maria: thanks. one more: add a section on schema evolution policy (how to do additive changes, deprecations). we've had surprises before.
Jen: and include a local dev story + docker-compose dev-proxy. that will reduce friction.
Sam: will include perf numbers and a quick envoy config used.
Aditya: great — moving this to RFC. if anything urgent, @Aditya DM. :thumbsup:
